memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. Randstad (RAND-NL) at EUR 35.42 (2026-10-09) is a cyclical recovery in temporary-staffing volumes at a generalist staffer with a slow self-help overlay, and it is not a compelling case: the shares have risen 55 percent in six months to the stock's own ten-year median multiple on consensus earnings that assume a gross-margin recovery the record rates as possible (about one in four for the full bull branch), not probable. The modal return is 10.0 percent a year over eighteen months and 8.1 percent over three years against the 20 percent bar. The park rule applies: business quality (E 2, BB 2) is D and the record does not argue past it, because the D rests on advantage and pricing power rather than on cyclical weakness. Management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4) is C, predictability (RA 8, E 2, BB 4) is B and trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) is B, so the case is parkable and trackable, not invalidated. Re-entry conditions named: a price near or below EUR 26 to EUR 31 (the modal path clearing 20 percent a year on three years and eighteen months respectively), or two consecutive quarters of group gross margin above 18.5 percent with permanent fees back in year-on-year growth, which would move the modal path toward the bull branch and the rating toward C or B. The compelling version of this case existed at EUR 21 to EUR 25 in the first half of 2026 and has been taken.
case: The thesis. Randstad is a cyclical recovery in temporary-staffing volumes at a generalist staffer with a slow self-help overlay, and at EUR 35.42 (2026-10-09) it is not compelling, because the shares have already risen 55 percent in six months to the ten-year median multiple on consensus earnings that assume a gross-margin recovery the record rates as possible, not probable. The modal return is about 10 percent a year over eighteen months and about 8 percent over three, half the bar.

The change is external and cyclical, and real. Temporary volumes turned after more than twelve quarters of market decline: organic revenue per working day -2.5 percent in FY2025, +0.4 percent in Q1 2026, +1.9 percent in Q2 2026; over 60 percent of regional markets growing in Q2 2026 (from 50 percent in Q1); the United States operational business +13 percent (a sixth consecutive quarter); Germany back to +4 percent; June exit rates ahead of the quarter and continuing into July; Adecco +5.6 percent organic and ManpowerGroup +6 percent. The own cycle is the one B among the external forces. The turn is in the lowest-margin third of the business (Operational +4 percent) while permanent fees, the high-margin line, still fell 5 percent; the sell-side expects only 2.7 to 3.3 percent organic growth in Q3 2026; the demand force does not meet the 'Demand Inflection' test of two-plus years of visibility (C). Competition (D: Adecco gaining share in 14 of 16 quarters and 160 basis points in Q2 2026, with pricing still rational), disruption (D: Indeed-OpenAI, Adecco's agentic AI on 50 percent of revenue, platforms at 10 percent markups against 35 to 65 percent) and the macro environment (D: a late-cycle rates squeeze turning into European credit stress, with 39 percent of revenue in Europe) are headwinds; regulation (C) and the supply side (C) are mixed. External forces C.

The internal change is a credible programme, not a step-change. Three forces are at B: strategy (four specialisations; EUR 500 million of technology capital; marketplaces at EUR 4 billion annualised revenue and 15 percent of volume against a 60 percent target), standards (EUR 100 million of structural savings; headcount 48,000 to 38,000; corporate FTEs -4 percent; Torc cutting cost per placement 50 percent), perimeter (the EUR 160 million LTM exit at about 10x EV/EBITA; Monster written to zero). The forces the framework weights most are absent: no chief-executive change (C, continuity; reappointed March 2026), no guidance increase (D; the 5 to 6 percent EBITA margin target unchanged since 2002 and defended at the AGM), no balance-sheet step-up (D; 1.8x and above the 1.0x threshold), shareholder returns held (C; EUR 1.62 floor; no buyback since 2024). The screen's rule is met at its lowest threshold. Internal forces C. 'Change Forces' C.
counter_case: At Building Block 1 and in the Written Summary, the strongest case against the D and the park is the bull case in its own words (ING, Bernstein, and the closing "other side" of the earnings review). The operating leverage of a right-sized staffer into a cyclical recovery is large and front-loaded. The cost base is now structurally lower: more than EUR 100 million of structural savings, headcount from 48,000 to 38,000, and a 3.1 percent margin held through three years of falling revenue prove it. The four-quarter recovery ratio is already 82 percent and the annualised conversion run-rate is 70 to 80 percent against a historical 40 to 50 percent, so incremental gross profit drops through at unprecedented rates; ING says the market is "too cautious on Randstad's conversion rates" and Bernstein expects mid-single-digit consensus EBITA upgrades. The digital marketplaces are three to four times as profitable as legacy delivery (Zorgwerk, Torc, the United States app) and are scaling at double digits a quarter (1.7 million self-scheduled shifts in Q2 2026; Torc cutting fill time and cost per placement by 50 percent). The LTM proceeds of EUR 0.91 a share fund a return. The balance sheet at 1.8x is the best in the peer group against Adecco's 2.7x and scrip dilution. If digital volume goes from 15 to 60 percent over 24 to 36 months, the group EBITA margin reaches 5 to 6 percent by 2028 even with the gross margin at 18 to 19 percent, FY2028 EPS approaches EUR 4.50, and the shares are worth about EUR 60 on a sector multiple of 11x EV/EBITA. The evidence for it is the Q2 2026 EBITA beat on a revenue beat, Germany and the United States inflecting, Zorgwerk growing 15 to 20 percent, and the sell-side's own target-price revisions of +21 percent in three months. The record concedes the cost discipline, the drop-through (its own modal EBITA margin rises to 3.3 percent by FY2028 on a flat gross margin), the marketplace unit economics at the unit level, the balance sheet, the credibility of the dividend floor, the probability of the volume turn, and that at a bottom-quartile multiple this would be a case to progress. It holds its view because, first, the bull case requires the gross margin to stop falling, and nothing in thirteen quarters, in the Q3 2026 guide, in the mix of the recovery (large accounts fastest, permanent fees -5 percent) or in client behaviour (asking to share efficiency gains) says it has; second, the 70 to 80 percent conversion run-rate is measured off a trough quarter against a cost base about to face euro-area wage inflation of 3.3 to 3.8 percent, so the 40 to 50 percent the company guides is the honest figure; third, the 5 to 6 percent target has been missed in every year since 2002, including 2021 to 2022 at 4.2 to 4.7 percent, and digital volume is 15 percent after EUR 500 million and four years; fourth, the price already carries consensus, which already carries a margin recovery, so the bull case has to be right twice (margin and re-rating) to deliver 20 percent a year, at joint odds of about one in four; fifth, Adecco is taking share with a better gross margin and more AI coverage, so even the recovery is arriving for the peer first. Where the case against would win: a gross margin above 18.5 percent for two consecutive quarters, the quarterly series that settles the case.

At Building Block 2, the case against the D is that the record is grading a cyclical at its trough: return on invested capital was 11.3 percent in a year of -2.5 percent organic growth, cash conversion was 165 percent of reported net income, leverage is 1.8x against Adecco's 2.7x, the dividend floor held, and the business took 16 percent of revenue out without a loss-making year, which is exactly the "medium or higher quality cyclical" the framework's 'Trough on Trough' pattern wants; on that reading business quality is a C and the park rule does not bite. The record concedes the resilience and the balance sheet and holds the D because the framework's business questions are about advantage and outputs, and on advantage the evidence runs the other way: the closest rival is taking share with a better gross margin, the large clients set price and terms, and on automated matching Randstad is a follower at 15 percent digital volume against Adecco's 50 percent agentic coverage. A resilient business without an advantage is a D on this framework; it is not a bad company.
triggers: - The series that settles the case: the group gross margin, quarterly. Above 18.5 percent for two consecutive quarters with permanent fees back in year-on-year growth moves the modal path toward the bull branch and the rating toward C or B. Alarm below 17.8 percent in Q3 2026 (as guided); Invalidate below 17.5 percent.

- Price re-entry: near or below EUR 31 (the modal path clearing 20 percent a year on eighteen months) or EUR 26 (on three years); the 'Trough on Trough' conditions would re-form in the range of the 52-week low of EUR 21.24.

- Volume: Alarm organic growth below 1 percent, or two consecutive months of Dutch, Belgian and United States temporary hours turning down, or a Q3 2026 print below 2 percent organic; Invalidate negative organic growth or Germany returning to a loss.
- Drop-through: Alarm the four-quarter recovery ratio falling toward 50 percent; Invalidate below 38 percent.

- Multiple: Alarm the sector giving back the July 2026 re-rating or the 200-day average turning down; Invalidate below the ten-year 10th-percentile band of 9.70x on unchanged earnings. What would make the re-rating earned rather than borrowed: estimates rising with the price.
- Macro: Alarm PMIs turning down for two months with temporary hours following; Invalidate negative organic growth across Europe.
